How does the 3–9 day national holiday affect domestic flights and coastal highways?

Ramazan Bayramı officially lasts three and a half days—starting at noon on Arefe (eve)—but when dates fall midweek, Turkish authorities often bridge adjacent working days into a 9-day break. In 2026, [Diyanet's official calendar](https://vakithesaplama.diyanet.gov.tr/dinigunler.php?yil=2026) sets Arefe on Thursday, March 19 and the three holiday days on Friday, March 20 through Sunday, March 22.

Even during a 3.5-day weekend, outbound highways from Istanbul toward Izmir, Bursa, and the Aegean coast back up sharply on Wednesday evening and Thursday afternoon. Domestic flights from Istanbul (IST/SAW) to Izmir, Bodrum, Dalaman, Antalya, and Kayseri routinely hit 95–100% load factors, with return bottlenecks peaking on Sunday afternoon and evening.

body.text: Are Istanbul museums, bazaars and hospitals open during Bayram?

State museums and municipal sites in Istanbul open late at 13:00 on Day 1 of Bayram and operate normally on Days 2 and 3, while the Grand Bazaar and Spice Bazaar close for the holiday. Public and private hospital emergency rooms stay open 24/7, but routine outpatient clinics and dental practices close or run reduced holiday rosters.

Specifically, [Turkish Ministry of Culture and Tourism sites](https://muze.gov.tr/duyuru-detay?Id=160) and [Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality museums](https://iisbf.gelisim.edu.tr/tr/akademik-bolum-turizm-rehberligi-haber-ramazan-bayrami-nda-istanbul-da-muze-ve-ziyaret-saatleri-aciklandi-turizm-rehberligi-icin-kritik-bilgilendirme) open at 13:00 on Day 1. Meanwhile, the [Grand Bazaar and Spice Bazaar](https://clevertourists.com/resources/istanbul-grand-bazaar-hours-guide) shut their gates during Ramazan Bayramı, and banks, post offices, and government agencies close from Thursday afternoon until Monday morning. Pharmacies operate via a rotating duty system (nöbetçi eczane). If you are planning elective procedures, review our [medical tourism coordination guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/services/medical-tourism) before locking clinic dates.
Why should foreign visitors book domestic legs months ahead if dates overlap?

Foreign travelers must lock in domestic flights, high-speed trains (YHT), and boutique hotels two to four months early whenever an itinerary overlaps with Ramazan Bayramı. Domestic demand drives airfares up to maximum fare buckets quickly, leaving late buyers with sold-out routes or costly business-class-only seats.

Because the Islamic lunar calendar shifts roughly 11 days earlier each year—moving Ramazan Bayramı to [March 9–11 in 2027](https://vakithesaplama.diyanet.gov.tr/icerik.php?icerik=154)—many international visitors overlook the dates until domestic legs are already full. Follow this preparation checklist:

items: Ticket domestic flights first: Secure Istanbul–Cappadocia, Istanbul–Izmir, or Antalya legs before finalizing non-refundable hotel stays.
Schedule bazaar visits before Arefe noon: Visit the Grand Bazaar and Spice Bazaar by Wednesday or Thursday morning before shutters drop.
Plan Day 1 morning outdoors: Walk along the Bosphorus, explore Balat, or take a morning ferry before museums open at 13:00.
Confirm private clinic follow-ups in writing: Verify post-op checkup coverage if your stay overlaps with Bayram weekend.
Keep cash and contactless cards ready: ATMs in resort towns occasionally run low on Turkish lira by Day 2.

body.text: What festive traditions and sweets will you encounter?

Known locally as Şeker Bayramı (Sugar Feast), Ramazan Bayramı centers on family reunions, paying respects to elders, and sharing sweets with guests. Visitors will notice lemon cologne (kolonya) offered at cafes and hotels, children greeting neighbors for wrapped candies, and pastry shops stacking trays of pistachio baklava, şöbiyet, and Turkish delight (lokum).

Many restaurants in Sultanahmet, Beyoğlu, and Kadıköy stay open throughout the holiday, though family-run neighborhood lokantas may close on Day 1. Greeting hosts with "İyi Bayramlar" (Happy Bayram) is warmly appreciated everywhere. faq.q: What are the exact 2026 Ramazan Bayramı dates in Türkiye?
faq.a: Per [Diyanet](https://diyanet.gov.tr/dini-gun-geceler), Arefe (half-day eve) is Thursday, March 19, 2026, and the three official holiday days run Friday, March 20 through Sunday, March 22, 2026.

faq.q: Do restaurants and cafes close during Ramazan Bayramı?
faq.a: Most hotels, tourist-area restaurants, and modern cafes remain open, especially from Day 1 afternoon onward. Small family-owned eateries may close on Day 1 morning.

faq.q: Can I visit Hagia Sophia and the Blue Mosque during Bayram?
faq.a: Active mosques hold morning Bayram prayers (Bayram namazı) shortly after sunrise on Day 1 and remain busy with worshippers. Plan non-worshipper visits for later in the day outside prayer times.

faq.q: Are ferries, trams, and metros running in Istanbul during Bayram?
faq.a: Yes. Istanbul public transit runs throughout the holiday—often on Sunday/holiday timetables and sometimes free for residents—making rail and ferries faster than taxis on busy afternoons.

faq.q: Will my private clinic or hospital perform surgery on Bayram?
faq.a: Emergency departments operate 24/7, but most elective surgeries and routine outpatient consultations pause during Bayram days. Always verify exact surgical and follow-up dates directly with your licensed medical team.
